mathematical_definition: For each of the trailing 60 fully-resolved historical start points t0, tracks the best favorable excursion (max forward close[j]-close[t0] over j in (t0,t0+10]) and best adverse excursion (max forward close[t0]-close[j]) within the sub_horizon=10-bar forward path; hist_path_asymmetry_60 is the ratio of the sums of those best-favorable and best-adverse excursions across all 60 windows (fav_sum/adv_sum) -- a LOCAL empirical measure of upside vs downside path asymmetry, distinct from any directional-return feature computed elsewhere (numba kernel first_passage_stats, window=60, sub_horizon=10, r_threshold_frac=0.001)
numerical_stability_notes: NaN whenever adv_sum <= 1e-12 (degenerate case: no adverse excursion at all across any of the 60 windows, e.g. a strictly monotone-up local history), a division-by-zero guard rather than a raw exception. Causality verified by direct code read during Phase 3 design (spec section 2): first_passage_stats's inner loop bound is t0 in [i-window-sub_horizon, i-sub_horizon) and j in (t0, t0+sub_horizon], so the maximum index ever read is j=i-1 -- every inner-loop index is strictly < i, no lookahead.
missing_value_policy: NaN for the first window+sub_horizon=70 bars, and NaN whenever adv_sum<=1e-12 (degenerate all-favorable window), never zero-filled
